terms.meaning: find the value(s) of the letter that make an equation true
a value of the letter that makes the equation true (also called a root)
an equation where the letter appears only to the power 1 (no x², no 1/x)
from a/b = c/d go straight to ad = cb; it's multiplying both sides by b and by d
two (or more) equations about the same unknowns, which must all be true at once
adding or subtracting whole equations so one unknown cancels out
rearrange one equation for one letter and put it into the other equation
equations that each give genuinely new information; you need as many as there are unknowns
an equation with x² as the highest power, e.g. x² + 6x + 5 = 0
if A × B = 0 then A = 0 or B = 0
x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a, the solutions of ax² + bx + c = 0; the roots are Chapter 12's pair with the sign flipped, divided by a
rewriting x² + bx + c as (x + b/2)² − (b/2)² + c; for a ≠ 1 take a out of the x terms first. Gives vertex form a(x + p)² + q
a quadratic written a(x + p)² + q; its vertex (turning point) is (−p, q)
a statement that one side is less than (<), greater than (>), at most (≤) or at least (≥) the other; its solution is a range of values

symbols.meaning: both the + version and the − version are answers
